issueOrPullRequest.title: Agent skills let Codex hot-poll long-running commands, burning a session in minutes
issueOrPullRequest.body:
The `commands/agents/` skills added in slice 925 were ported from their Claude twins with the **arguments** rewritten (D3) but the **control flow** carried over unchanged. Under Claude Code that flow is free: `Bash` blocks until a command exits, so a long review is one turn. Under Codex it is not — the model stays in an agentic loop while the command runs, and every check-is-it-done turn is a full round trip carrying the whole conversation.

**Observed:** `$sq-review code 925` in a Codex session consumed an entire 5-hour session allowance in roughly 10–15 minutes of wall clock — about as long as the review itself takes. The session appeared to be "constantly checking for the review", generating tokens the user never saw. This is hot polling, not a slow command.

Reported independently: a developer hit the same wall using Astra in GitHub Copilot with no squadron involved, which suggests this is general agent-harness behavior rather than anything specific to our CLI.

**Two skills are implicated:**

- `commands/agents/sq-review/SKILL.md` — says run the review and show the result. `sq review` blocks for minutes; nothing tells the model to run it once and wait rather than poll.
- `commands/agents/sq-run/SKILL.md` — worse, and structural. It carries the Claude command's explicit multi-step loop verbatim, including `loop back to the Main Loop`. Every pipeline step repeats the `sq-review` failure mode. This one has not been exercised live; based on the review result it would be more expensive, not less.

The shorter skills (`sq-list`, `sq-auth`, `sq-spawn`, …) are fine — their commands return immediately.

**What this needs**

1. A standing "running commands under Codex" rule carried by every `sq-*` skill: run the command **once**, in the foreground, read its exit. Do not re-run it, do not poll for completion, do not check whether it finished between turns.
2. For `sq-review`: state plainly that `sq review` blocks and prints its own progress, so a single invocation is the whole interaction.
3. For `sq-run`: reconsider the in-skill loop. The agentic loop it describes assumes a harness where model turns are free; in Codex they are billed. Running one step per invocation, with the user re-invoking, moves the loop back to the user where it costs nothing. `sq-run` stays in the agents tree — the bijection drift test keeps a twin for every Claude command, and that is the right invariant.

**Caveat on scope:** this is inferred from one observed session plus the design of the files. Before writing the fix, someone should confirm what Codex actually does with a blocking command — whether the polling comes from the skill's wording, from Codex's own loop, or both. If it is purely Codex-side, the wording fix may not be sufficient and the answer may be that long-running commands should not be skill-invoked at all.

**Workaround until fixed:** run `sq review …` from the terminal and point Codex at the saved review file.

Found during slice 925 live verification (Task 9, step 6). The skill invocation itself worked correctly — Codex offered `$sq-review`, parsed `code 925` from prose, and ran `sq review code 925`. The defect is in what happens while the command runs.

nodes.body:
Mechanism confirmed from Codex source (rust-v0.146.1, `codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/`):

- `unified_exec` is on by default except on Windows. `exec_command` waits `yield_time_ms` (default 10000, clamped 250–30000) and then returns a session ID if the command is still running.
- The model finishes by polling `write_stdin` with empty `chars`. An empty poll's wait is clamped to 5000 ms minimum and `background_terminal_max_timeout` maximum (default 300000).
- Each poll is a full model turn. A 10-minute review polled at the 5 s floor is ~120 billed round trips; at 300 s it's 2–3.

So the skill wording was the cause, not something only Codex could fix. Commit 2127739b adds an identical "Waiting on the command" section to `sq-review`, `sq-run`, `sq-task` and `sq-pr`: run the command once, wait on the session with empty `write_stdin` and `yield_time_ms: 300000`, and do nothing between waits. A test keeps the four copies identical.

Still open:
1. Live check. `$sq-review code <n>` in Codex after `sq install-commands --ide codex` should show a handful of polls, not a stream.
2. `sq-run`'s in-skill loop (item 3). The waiting rule covers its review and dispatch commands, which were the expensive part. Whether the loop should instead run one step per invocation is a separate call.

Both open items resolved.

**Live Codex verification (item 1):** confirmed via `codex` session status before/after two `sq review` runs (including one long kimi-k2.7 run) — combined cost was ~1% of the 7-day limit and left 89% of the 5-hour limit intact, versus the original report of a single review burning an entire 5-hour session in 10-15 minutes. The waiting-rule fix (2127739b) holds up in practice.

**sq-run loop restructuring (item 2):** re-read `commands/agents/sq-run/SKILL.md` end to end. The loop's turn count scales with actual pipeline work — one turn per step-fetch, one per action executed (cf-op/dispatch/review/checkpoint/commit/summary/devlog), one per step-done — not with wall-clock wait time. The expensive sub-commands it shells out to (`sq run --prompt-only`, `sq review`, dispatch) already carry the shared waiting-rule section, so they don't hot-poll either. This is a structurally different shape from the original hot-poll bug: turns are proportional to real work, not to how long a command takes to finish. No evidence surfaced of it burning excess budget in practice. Closing as resolved; reopen with a concrete transcript if it turns up in the wild.
